design.title: Pirate Cutlass
design.tagline: A proper captain's cutlass with a curved knuckle guard — ready for the high seas!
materials: Corrugated cardboard — one large box (double-wall is best for the blade)
White glue or hot glue
String or cloth tape for the grip wrap (optional)
Paint or markers to decorate (optional)

fitChecks.reason: blade top layer must be narrower than the blade so a flat rim shows along both edges
blade top layer must fit within the sword's length with room for the grip
knuckle guard strip must be long enough to curve from crossguard to pommel (4-inch chord plus the bow of the C)

steps.title: Print, tape and trace

figures.caption: Sword Body — trace TWICE.
Blade Top Layer — trace TWICE.
Knuckle Guard strip — trace ONCE.

instructions: Print the template at 100% actual size and tape the pages together using the grid.
Trace the Sword Body TWICE, the Blade Top Layer TWICE, and the Knuckle Guard ONCE onto cardboard.
Keep the corrugation arrows lined up with the little waves inside the cardboard — that makes the blade strong.
steps.check: You should have 5 pencil outlines: 2 big swords, 2 slim blade layers, 1 slitted strip.
steps.tip: Trace on the plain side of the cardboard so pencil lines are easy to see.

steps.title: Cut out the parts

figures.caption: Your full cut list — 5 pieces. Dashed lines are NOT cuts: score them half-deep only.

instructions: Grown-up job: cut along all solid lines with a sharp knife and metal ruler, in 2–3 light passes.
Kids can help by holding the ruler and peeling the offcuts.
Do NOT cut the dashed lines — those get scored lightly (half-deep) for folding and wrapping.
steps.check: 5 cut pieces, and every dashed line is still uncut on the front face.

steps.title: Glue the two body layers

figures.caption: Glue covers the whole first sword; the second sword stacks straight onto it, edges matching all around.

instructions: Cover one Sword Body with a thin layer of white glue, right to the edges.
Stack the second Sword Body on top, lining up the pommel, crossguard and blade tip exactly.
Press it flat under a stack of books while it dries — this makes the blade stiff and straight.
steps.check: Edges line up all around with no layer sticking out, and the blade does not flex when you wave it.
steps.tip: In a hurry? A grown-up can use hot glue in a zigzag instead — press for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the blade top layers

figures.caption: The Blade Top lands on the dashed outline — centered on the blade, tip matching the sword tip. Flip the sword and repeat on the back.

instructions: Glue one Blade Top Layer down the middle of the blade on the front side — the dashed outline in the diagram shows exactly where it lands.
Flip the sword over and glue the second one on the back, in the same spot.
Line each layer's tip up with the blade tip — an even strip of flat blade, about a finger wide, should show along both edges.
steps.check: The blade has a raised ridge down the middle on BOTH sides, and all three tips meet at one point.

steps.title: Bend and attach the knuckle guard

arrows.label: crease each slit to curl it

figures.caption: Crease every slit so the flat strip curls into a big C, slits on the inside of the curve.
The C bridges from the underside of the crossguard up to the pommel — hot-glue both ends where the arrows point.

instructions: Crease each dashed slit on the Knuckle Guard with your fingernail so the strip curves smoothly — slits face IN, toward your fingers.
Hot-glue one end to the underside of the crossguard, on the side your fingers wrap.
Curve it around and glue the other end to the pommel (the round knob at the top of the grip).
Hold each end for 30 seconds while the glue sets. Grown-up job — hot glue is HOT!
steps.check: Your fingers fit comfortably between the grip and the guard, and both glued ends hold when you tug gently.

steps.title: Wrap the grip and decorate

figures.caption: The finished cutlass: string-wrapped grip, curved knuckle guard, decorated blade.

instructions: Wrap string or cloth tape around the grip, following the scored diagonal lines — it looks great and feels grippy.
Paint the blade silver or gray, the guard gold, and the grip brown or black.
Captain's touch: draw a skull, an anchor, or your ship's name on the blade!
steps.check: The wrap doesn't slide when you squeeze the grip — you're ready to set sail!
steps.tip: Acrylic paint works, but markers are faster and never warp the cardboard.

steps.check: The wrap doesn't slide when you squeeze the grip — you're ready to set sail!
steps.tip: Acrylic paint works, but markers are faster and never warp the cardboard.

design.title: Pirate Cutlass
design.tagline: A proper captain's cutlass with a curved knuckle guard — ready for the high seas!
materials: Corrugated cardboard — one large box (double-wall is best for the blade)
White glue or hot glue
String or cloth tape for the grip wrap (optional)
Paint or markers to decorate (optional)

fitChecks.reason: blade top layer must be narrower than the blade so a flat rim shows along both edges
blade top layer must fit within the sword's length with room for the grip
knuckle guard strip must be long enough to curve from crossguard to pommel (4-inch chord plus the bow of the C)

steps.title: Print, tape and trace

figures.caption: Sword Body — trace TWICE.
Blade Top Layer — trace TWICE.
Knuckle Guard strip — trace ONCE.

instructions: Print the template at 100% actual size and tape the pages together using the grid.
Trace the Sword Body TWICE, the Blade Top Layer TWICE, and the Knuckle Guard ONCE onto cardboard.
Keep the corrugation arrows lined up with the little waves inside the cardboard — that makes the blade strong.
steps.check: You should have 5 pencil outlines: 2 big swords, 2 slim blade layers, 1 slitted strip.
steps.tip: Trace on the plain side of the cardboard so pencil lines are easy to see.

steps.title: Cut out the parts

figures.caption: Your full cut list — 5 pieces. Dashed lines are NOT cuts: score them half-deep only.

instructions: Grown-up job: cut along all solid lines with a sharp knife and metal ruler, in 2–3 light passes.
Kids can help by holding the ruler and peeling the offcuts.
Do NOT cut the dashed lines — those get scored lightly (half-deep) for folding and wrapping.
steps.check: 5 cut pieces, and every dashed line is still uncut on the front face.

steps.title: Glue the two body layers

figures.caption: Glue covers the whole first sword; the second sword stacks straight onto it, edges matching all around.

instructions: Cover one Sword Body with a thin layer of white glue, right to the edges.
Stack the second Sword Body on top, lining up the pommel, crossguard and blade tip exactly.
Press it flat under a stack of books while it dries — this makes the blade stiff and straight.
steps.check: Edges line up all around with no layer sticking out, and the blade does not flex when you wave it.
steps.tip: In a hurry? A grown-up can use hot glue in a zigzag instead — press for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the blade top layers

figures.caption: The Blade Top lands on the dashed outline — centered on the blade, tip matching the sword tip. Flip the sword and repeat on the back.

instructions: Glue one Blade Top Layer down the middle of the blade on the front side — the dashed outline in the diagram shows exactly where it lands.
Flip the sword over and glue the second one on the back, in the same spot.
Line each layer's tip up with the blade tip — an even strip of flat blade, about a finger wide, should show along both edges.
steps.check: The blade has a raised ridge down the middle on BOTH sides, and all three tips meet at one point.

steps.title: Bend and attach the knuckle guard

arrows.label: crease each slit to curl it

figures.caption: Crease every slit so the flat strip curls into a big C, slits on the inside of the curve.
The C bridges from the underside of the crossguard up to the pommel — hot-glue both ends where the arrows point.

instructions: Crease each dashed slit on the Knuckle Guard with your fingernail so the strip curves smoothly — slits face IN, toward your fingers.
Hot-glue one end to the underside of the crossguard, on the side your fingers wrap.
Curve it around and glue the other end to the pommel (the round knob at the top of the grip).
Hold each end for 30 seconds while the glue sets. Grown-up job — hot glue is HOT!
steps.check: Your fingers fit comfortably between the grip and the guard, and both glued ends hold when you tug gently.

steps.title: Wrap the grip and decorate

figures.caption: The finished cutlass: string-wrapped grip, curved knuckle guard, decorated blade.

instructions: Wrap string or cloth tape around the grip, following the scored diagonal lines — it looks great and feels grippy.
Paint the blade silver or gray, the guard gold, and the grip brown or black.
Captain's touch: draw a skull, an anchor, or your ship's name on the blade!
steps.check: The wrap doesn't slide when you squeeze the grip — you're ready to set sail!
steps.tip: Acrylic paint works, but markers are faster and never warp the cardboard.
